item.title: Identification, Monitoring, and Management of Elevated Ketones in Ambulatory Settings: A Consensus Statement
item.description:
Importance: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), although preventable in most cases, is a leading cause of hospitalization in people with insulin-treated diabetes and is associated with suboptimal glycemic outcomes, increased risk for diabetes complications, and increased health care expenditure. This consensus statement outlines factors that may help identify individuals with diabetes who are at increased risk for elevated ketone levels; provides recommendations for ketone monitoring, including potential testing modalities; and discusses appropriate testing frequency and self-management strategies based on ketone severity.

Objective: To develop a clinical decision algorithm on the detection, monitoring, and management of elevated ketones in children, adolescents, and nonpregnant adults with diabetes.

Evidence review: For this consensus statement, 2 members of the American Diabetes Association Evidence Synthesis Team convened a panel of 13 external experts in diabetes, including clinicians, researchers, and certified diabetes care and education specialists, from May to October 2025. to systematically search PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, The Lens, and Semantic Scholar without date limits for literature on detecting ketones in people with diabetes. Relevant results were combined with citation searching and summarized; supplemental searches were also conducted for specific questions raised by the panel. The nominal group method was used for consensus and recommendations. Data were analyzed from October 2025 to January 2026.

Findings: Several factors may help identify people with diabetes who are at increased risk for elevated ketone levels, including those who require insulin therapy, who have a history of elevated hemoglobin A1c or episodes of DKA in the past year, or whose treatment regimen includes use of either an insulin pump or sodium glucose cotransporter inhibitor therapy. Situations that should prompt ketone monitoring, including prolonged hyperglycemia, dehydration, or nausea or vomiting, are reviewed along with ketone testing modalities, including capillary, urine, and emerging continuous ketone sensing technologies. A framework to allow people with diabetes to self-manage elevated ketones is presented, which grounds treatment based on ketone severity and specifies frequency of monitoring.

Conclusions and relevance: The algorithm presented in this consensus statement is meant to assist with early ketone detection and prevention of DKA. It is intended for health care professionals, policymakers, researchers, and developers of ketone monitoring tools to support current care while providing a foundation for future clinical applications as technologies evolve.

Shah VN, Bannuru RR, Durnwald C, El Sayed N, Klonoff DC, Kruger D

item.title: Simplified Regimen for Hypertension Management With Telemedicine and Blood Pressure Self-Monitoring: A Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Hypertension control remains difficult despite effective medications, motivating integrated remote-management strategies.

Objective: To test whether home blood pressure (BP) monitoring (HBPM), telemedicine, clinician-supervised titration, and single-pill combination (SPC) delivery improve office BP compared with usual care.

Design, setting, and participants: This open-label, multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolled adults aged 18 to 75 years with treated essential hypertension who met protocol-defined office BP thresholds at screening at 4 Chinese medical centers from January 1, 2021, through July 20, 2023. Participants were randomized 1:1. Data were analyzed from December 18, 2025, through February 10, 2026, based on modified intention to treat.

Interventions: All participants received a free HBPM device and a 2-week equivalent SPC run-in. After randomization, both groups continued HBPM; the intervention group also received telemedicine review, clinician-supervised titration, and free medication and delivery.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in office systolic BP (SBP) from baseline, assessed after the run-in and at randomization, to 6 months, analyzed using an independent-samples t test. Secondary outcomes included office diastolic BP (DBP), rate of BP control, and adverse events.

Results: Among 364 participants (mean [SD] age, 54 [11] years; 195 male [53.6%]), 180 were randomized to the intervention group and 184 to usual care. A total of 163 intervention participants and 172 usual care participants had baseline and 6-month SBP data. Office SBP decreased by a mean (SD) of 9.7 (16.5) mm Hg in the intervention group and 5.8 (16.8) mm Hg in usual care (between-group difference, -3.9 [95% CI, -7.5 to -0.3] mm Hg; P = .03). Office DBP decreased by a mean (SD) of 4.2 (11.1) vs 1.1 (11.8) mm Hg (difference, -3.1 [95% CI, -5.6 to -0.7] mm Hg; P = .02). Office BP was controlled in 132 of 180 participants (73.3%) for the intervention vs 124 of 184 (67.4%) for usual care (P = .27). Adverse events occurred in 24 of 180 intervention participants (13.3%) vs 15 of 184 usual care participants (8.2%) (P = .13), and adverse event-related treatment discontinuation occurred in 15 (8.3%) vs 1 (0.5%), respectively (P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In this randomized clinical trial of adults with treated essential hypertension and elevated office BP at screening, the integrated intervention produced a modestly greater reduction in office BP than usual care at 6 months. Longer-term and implementation studies are needed to evaluate the closed-loop remote management pathway.

Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry Identifier: ChiCTR2000037217.

Maimaitiaili R, Han J, Wan M, Shi J, Wang M, Zhao F

item.title: Food Insecurity During Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopmental Outcomes
item.description:
Importance: Food insecurity affects over 12% of adults in the US and has been associated with adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes. However, little is known about the relationship between food insecurity during pregnancy and child neurodevelopmental outcomes.

Objective: To determine whether food insecurity during pregnancy is associated with greater risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) including autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study included pregnant individuals in the Kaiser Permanente Northern California integrated health system surveyed between June 2020 and September 2022 and their children followed up through December 2025.

Exposures: Food insecurity measured using the Hunger as a Vital Sign Questionnaire.

Main outcomes and measures: NDD and ASD diagnoses were determined by the presence of International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9) and International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes in child electronic health records. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) for any NDD and ASD diagnoses were estimated separately using Cox models adjusted for maternal age, neighborhood deprivation index, insurance type, parity, prepregnancy body mass index, prepregnancy depression, child birth year, and sex. Participation in food assistance programs was evaluated as a modifier of the association between food insecurity and NDD risk.

Results: Of a total 21 376 pregnant individuals who responded, 13 285 met criteria for inclusion in analysis (mean [SD] age at delivery, 32.7 [4.5] years; 2781 Asian [20.9%], 410 Black [3.1%], 2628 Hispanic [19.8%], 6505 White [49.0%]); 1599 (12.0%) reported food insecurity. Of the children in the cohort (6835 male [51.4%]), 2741 (20.6%) were diagnosed with NDD and 690 (5.2%) with ASD. Food insecurity during pregnancy was associated with greater risk of both any NDD (aHR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.10-1.38) and ASD (aHR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.21-1.80). Risk was elevated only among those who did not receive food assistance both for NDD (no food assistance: aHR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.43; food assistance: aHR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.80-1.34) and ASD (no food assistance: aHR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.36-2.10; food assistance: aHR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.49-1.22).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of mother-child pairs in a Northern California health system, food insecurity during pregnancy was associated with greater risk of NDDs. Participation in food assistance programs by households that experience food insecurity may provide health benefits for children; children born to households experiencing food insecurity may benefit from earlier developmental screening and monitoring.

Grosvenor LP, Chehab RF, Al-Khatib NA, Anderson M, Ames JL, Ferrara A

item.title: Clinical Cutoff Scores for the Problematic Media Use Measure in the ABCD Study
item.description:
Importance: Dysregulated digital media use that interferes with functioning, or problematic media use (PMU), is a growing concern for child development. Although measures can capture PMU as a dimensional construct, scales lack risk cutoffs for early adolescents (aged 11-15 years).

Objective: To establish cutoff scores for the Problematic Media Use Measure (PMUM) and examine criterion validity.

Design, setting, and participants: This longitudinal cohort study with a 4-year follow-up analyzed data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, release 6.0. The cohort represented ABCD Study adolescents with follow-up data for waves 2 through 5; the longitudinal sample included adolescents with PMUM data at all 4 waves.

Exposures: Problematic media use as measured by developed PMUM cutoff scores.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary outcomes included parent-reported internalizing and externalizing symptoms, measured using the Child Behavior Checklist, and academic performance, measured by parent-reported grades over the past year. Four time points were analyzed in July 2026: time 1, 2019 to 2020 (age 11-12 years); time 2, 2020 to 2021 (age 12-13 years); time 3, 2021 to 2022 (age 13-14 years); and time 4, 2022 to 2023 (age 14-15 years). Item response theory was used to establish cutoff scores. Longitudinal models were used to examine criterion validity.

Results: At time 1, the cohort included 10 435 adolescents aged 11 to 12 years (5465 male [52.4%]). Cross-sectional samples were 9749, 9033, and 8262 participants at times 2, 3, and 4, respectively. A total of 6623 completed all 4 time points. Cutoff scores for PMUM were 9 to 22 for the not-at-risk level, 23 to 34 for the at-risk level, and 35 to 45 for the high-risk level. Applying the PMUM cutoff scores cross-sectionally, high-risk prevalence was stable across waves (time 1, 642 participants [6.2%]; time 2, 649 participants [6.7%]; time 3, 592 participants [6.6%]; time 4, 543 participants [6.6%]), and at-risk prevalence declined (time 1, 3677 participants [35.2%]; time 2, 3238 participants [33.2%]; time 3, 2902 participants [32.1%]; time 4, 2554 participants [30.9%]). Risk groups differed on outcomes at every wave. Averaged across the 4 waves, median (IQR) internalizing symptom T scores were 45 (38-52) for the not-at-risk group, 51 (44-58) for the at-risk group, and 57 (48-65) for the high-risk group; median (IQR) externalizing symptom T scores were 40 (34-46), 46 (40-54), and 55 (46-62), respectively; and median (IQR) grades were 4 (3-4), 4 (3-4), and 3 (2-4), respectively (all P < .001). In the criterion lagged model adjusting for the prior outcome and sex, the at-risk classification estimated next-wave internalizing symptoms (b = 0.12 [95% CI, 0.10-0.15]), externalizing symptoms (b = 0.13 [95% CI, 0.11-0.15]), and grades (b = -0.08 [95% CI, -0.10 to -0.05]) (all P < .001), and high risk classification showed more pronounced associations (internalizing symptoms: b = 0.22 [95% CI, 0.18-0.27]; externalizing symptoms: b = 0.22 [0.18-0.27]; grades: b = -0.19 [95% CI, -0.24 to -0.15] (all P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: This cohort study of adolescents showed that PMUM cutoff scores were prospectively associated with behavioral, emotional, and academic outcomes across 4 annual waves of the ABCD Study. These thresholds may be useful for identifying adolescents at greatest need for intervention.

Falcione K, McDaniel BT, Magis-Weinberg L, Emond J, Domoff SE

item.title: Maternal Prepregnancy Body Mass Index and Developmental Vulnerability at 36 Months
item.description:
Importance: Maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) is increasingly relevant in Asia, but its association with domain-specific developmental vulnerability in early childhood remains unclear.

Objective: To investigate the associations of maternal prepregnancy BMI with multidomain and domain-specific developmental vulnerability (DV) at age 3 years.

Design, setting, and participants: This prospective, nationally representative cohort study used 6-month and 36-month follow-up data from the 2005 Taiwan Birth Cohort. Data analysis was performed from February to June 2026. Of 21 248 mother-child pairs at baseline, 18 577 complete-case pairs were analyzed at 36 months after excluding multiple births, participants lost to follow-up, and those with missing covariate or milestone data.

Exposures: Self-reported maternal prepregnancy BMI was categorized by Taiwan Health Promotion Administration criteria as underweight (<18.5), normal weight (18.5-23.9), overweight (24.0-26.9), and obesity (≥27.0). Covariates, including maternal sociodemographic characteristics, pregnancy and perinatal outcomes, and paternal BMI, were selected using a directed acyclic graph.

Main outcomes and measures: Child DV was defined as milestone nonattainment beyond cohort-specific empirical thresholds (greater than 90th percentile) at 36 months, based on caregiver-reported sentinel milestones collected during structured home visits. DV is a population-level screening indicator, not a clinical diagnosis of developmental delay. Multidomain DV (MDV) was defined as DV in greater than or equal to 2 of 5 domains.

Results: Among the 18 577 mother-child pairs analyzed (maternal mean [SD] age, 28.85 [4.83] years; female infants, 8849 [47.6%]; mean [SD] gestational age, 38.38 [1.52] weeks; maternal underweight, 3725 [20.1%]; normal weight, 12 180 [65.6%]; overweight, 1659 [8.9%]; obesity, 1013 [5.4%]), MDV showed a U-shaped pattern across maternal BMI categories. Compared with normal weight, maternal underweight was associated with a higher risk of MDV (adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 1.19; 95% CI, 1.06-1.33). Maternal obesity was associated more clearly with language-domain vulnerability (aRR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.25-1.94) than with MDV after adjustment (aRR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.97-1.54). Mediation analyses suggested limited mediation by recorded gestational complications.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 18 577 mother-child pairs in Taiwan, maternal underweight was associated with a higher risk of MDV at 36 months, while maternal obesity was associated more clearly with language-domain vulnerability than with overall MDV. These findings suggested that preconception weight optimization and developmental surveillance warranted consideration of both extremes of maternal BMI.

Huang YD, Huang YS, Chen HC, Luo YR, Lee MC, Liao MY
Journal Article

item.title: Neonatal Care Length of Stay and Physiological Readiness for Discharge in Preterm Newborns
item.description:
Importance: Preterm neonates need long hospital stays. Unnecessarily prolonged hospitalization can worsen outcomes, exacerbate parental stress, and increase costs of care.

Objective: To identify the postmenstrual age (PMA) when preterm neonates reach physiological maturity for discharge (breathing without support, feeding orally, and weighing ≥1700 g), the PMA at discharge from neonatal care, and the number of care days between physiological readiness and discharge.

Design, setting, and participants: This multicenter, population-based cohort study used the UK National Neonatal Research Database and included all neonatal units in England and Wales (data from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2023, were analyzed between June 2024 and June 2025). Participants were hospitalized preterm neonates (<37 weeks' gestational age [GA]) without a lethal congenital anomaly who were admitted for at least 48 hours and survived to discharge home.

Main outcomes and measures: PMA at physiological readiness for discharge and at discharge and the number of days of difference between the 2.

Results: There were 238 563 neonates (129 671 [54.4%] males), with median GA of 34 weeks (IQR, 32-35 weeks) and birth weight of 2090 g (IQR, 1635-2508 g). Overall, 19.5% (60.7% of those born at 22-24 weeks' GA) were discharged before reaching physiological readiness. Among the remaining neonates, the median PMA at physiological readiness was 36 (IQR, 35-36) weeks. This was later in more premature neonates (40 [IQR, 38-42] weeks in those born at 22-24 weeks' GA vs 35 [IQR, 35-36] weeks in those born at >31 weeks' GA). Overall, neonates stayed in the hospital for a median of 2 (IQR, 1-4) days after reaching physiological readiness. This difference was longer in more premature neonates: 4 (IQR, 1-7) days in those born at 22 to 24 weeks' GA, 4 (IQR, 2-7) days in those born at 25 to 27 weeks, 3 (IQR, 2-6) days in those born at 28 to 31 weeks, and 2 (IQR, 1-4) days in those born at more than 32 weeks. Overall, median (IQR) length of stay decreased with increasing birth GA: for neonates born at 22 to 24 weeks' GA, it was 125 (IQR, 109-144) days; at 25 to 29 weeks, 89 (IQR, 75-106) days; at 28 to 31 weeks, 45 (IQR, 35-59) days; at 32 to 33 weeks, 21 (IQR, 16-27) days; and at 34 to 36 weeks, 8 (IQR, 4-13) days.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, neonates born more preterm achieved physiological readiness for discharge at higher PMAs and had longer periods in the hospital after reaching physiological readiness. The findings suggest that research and services should focus on clinical measures of discharge readiness and incorporate parental and social factors and inequity to optimize length of stay without unintended adverse impact on family stress.

Tao S, Szatkowski L, Seaton SE, Abramson J, Arellano-Meza M, Harvey J

item.title: Polygenic Risk Scores and PSA Levels for Risk of Prostate Cancer and Related Mortality
item.description:
Importance: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing is the standard method for prostate screening and long-term risk assessment. Given the high heritability for prostate cancer (PCa), genetic factors may provide additional value.

Objective: To inform risk-stratified PCa screening strategies beyond PSA alone by integrating genetic risk.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study included individuals from the Stockholm3 (STHLM3) study, a prospective, population-based screening trial that enrolled men aged 50 to 69 years in Stockholm, Sweden, between May 2012 and December 2014. Of 59 088 eligible men without prior PCa who consented, 59 067 with a valid PSA test were included. PCa outcomes were recorded from inclusion until December 31, 2023. Data were analyzed from April 2025 to January 2026.

Exposures: Men were categorized by baseline PSA level and genetic risk; first-degree family history of PCa was assessed for all, while a 232-variant polygenic risk score (PRS) was calculated for those with PSA levels of 1 ng/mL or greater, per trial design.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcomes were clinically significant disease (defined as International Society of Urological Pathology grade ≥2) and PCa-specific mortality. Cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 2-, 6-, and 10-year absolute risks were stratified by PSA level at entry and genetic risk and estimated using regression standardization.

Results: Among the 59 067 individuals included in the analysis, the median age at inclusion was 60.6 (IQR, 55.1-65.7) years. The 10-year risk of clinically significant disease was 0.5% among men with PSA level less than 1 ng/mL and doubled with a positive family history (HR, 2.38 [95% CI, 1.57-3.59]). For PSA levels of 1 to 3 ng/mL, the 10-year risk was 5.9%, tripling in the PRS category of greater than 80% to 100% compared with PRS category of 0 to 20% (HR, 3.53 [95% CI, 2.36-5.28]). For PSA levels of 3 ng/mL or greater, the 10-year risk was 21%, with a similar PRS association (HR, 2.31 [95% CI, 1.86-2.86]). PRS category of greater than 80% to 100% was associated with higher PCa-specific mortality (HR, 2.71 [95% CI, 1.19-6.16]). Based on absolute risks, several genetic groups exceeded established thresholds for further investigation.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 59 067 men from the STHLM3 study, a PRS and family history provided meaningful 10-year risk stratification for clinically significant disease and PCa-specific death for men with PSA levels of 1 ng/mL or greater, suggesting that genetic information may contribute to risk refinement within PSA-based screening for PCa.

Mariaz M, Micoli C, Foley GR, Palm EE, Discacciati A, Vigneswaran HT

item.title: Subsidies and Behavioral Interventions to Increase Online Fruit and Vegetable Purchasing: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: The US population eats less than the recommended amounts of fruits and vegetables despite known health benefits. Innovative solutions to increase fruits and vegetables purchasing are needed.

Objective: To examine whether fruits and vegetables subsidies, choice architecture, and/or loss-framed text message reminders increase fruits and vegetables purchases in an online shopping store.

Design, setting, and participants: This 3-month pilot randomized clinical trial (October 24, 2024, and January 21, 2025) assessed individuals from the University of Pennsylvania Health System aged 30 to 70 years with a body mass index of 30 or greater and a hemoglobin A1c level greater than 8% who were comfortable shopping online and had a credit or debit card. Each participant participated for 3 months, but recruitment was rolling. The first participant was enrolled on October 24, 2024, and the last participant finished all study procedures on June 18, 2025. The last participant was enrolled January 27, 2025. The study used the online shopping platform Instacart.

Intervention: Participants were randomized to 1 of 5 arms: (1) control ($20 per month coupon on the study's online shopping platform), (2) subsidy ($160 per month for fruits and vegetables on the study's online shopping platform), (3) subsidy plus choice architecture (fruits and vegetables appear first on storefront), (4) subsidy plus salience (weekly loss-framed text messages about subsidy balance), or (5) subsidy plus salience plus choice architecture.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary outcome was total expenditures on fruits and vegetables on the study's online shopping platform. Secondary outcomes were (1) mean percentage of subsidy used across 3 months, (2) cumulative percentage of fruits and vegetables expenditures, and (3) change in HbA1c level. Analyses used either the intention-to-treat population or participants who activated their shopping memberships (per-protocol population).

Results: Of 1070 individuals assessed, 210 (129 [61.4%] female) were included in the study. Mean (SD) age of the study participants was 51.6 (10.8) years, and mean (SD) body mass index was 37.99 (7.28). Participants in the intention-to-treat group who received the subsidy spent a monthly mean of $92.52 (95% CI, $74.15-$110.90; P < .001) more on fruits and vegetables on the study's online shopping platform than the control group. Cumulative fruits and vegetables expenditure as a percentage of total expenditures was 21.47 percentage points (95% CI, 8.68-34.27 percentage points; P = .001) higher in the subsidy vs control arm. After 3 months, subsidy recipients vs control participants had a nonsignificant -0.28% (95% CI, -1.11% to 0.56%; P = .51) decrease in HbA1c level. In the per-protocol group, those receiving vs not receiving salience spent $18.83 (95% CI, $4.73-$32.92; P = .009) more on fruits and vegetables monthly. Choice architecture did not have a significant effect.

Conclusions and relevance: In this pilot randomized clinical trial of fruits and vegetables subsidies, choice architecture, and/or loss-framed text message reminders in an online store, providing a $160-monthly subsidy increased fruits and vegetables purchasing. Once participants activated memberships, weekly reminders of the subsidy balance but not choice architecture significantly increased fruits and vegetables spending.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06283394.

Hua SV, Putt M, Coratti S, White J, Hossain M, Posner H

item.title: Buprenorphine Use and State-Level Prior Authorization Changes in Medicaid
item.description:
Importance: To increase access to medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD), such as buprenorphine, several states have implemented laws limiting prior authorization requirements for MOUD in Medicaid plans.

Objective: To evaluate the association between state laws limiting preauthorization requirements for MOUD in Medicaid plans and buprenorphine use.

Design, setting, and participants: This repeated cross-sectional, difference-in-differences study examined buprenorphine prescriptions for Medicaid patients aged 15 to 64 years during January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2020. Data were derived from the IQVIA Longitudinal Prescription Database (including 94% of US prescriptions) and IQVIA Formulary Impact Analyzer (a pharmacy transactions database). Analyses included 13 treatment states that implemented laws during 2015 to 2019 and 25 control states that did not enact laws during 2014 to 2020. Data were analyzed between January 5 and May 11, 2026.

Exposure: Laws limiting prior authorization requirements.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcomes were monthly buprenorphine dispensing rates and initiation rates (number of patients with buprenorphine prescriptions and new prescriptions per 1000 Medicaid enrollees) and monthly dispensing gaps (days between the date prescriptions were written and dispensed). Subgroup analyses were conducted among states with high or low baseline prior authorization rejection rates, defined as the frequency of buprenorphine prescription rejection due to prior authorization requirements during the 12 months before law implementation (treatment states) or during 2014 (control states).

Results: Sample sizes varied by outcome: dispensing rate, 12 697 583 prescriptions for 652 035 patients (mean [SD] age at the time of a claim, 37.6 [9.5] years; 327 493 female [50.2%]), initiation rate, 723 592 new prescriptions for 588 940 patients (mean [SD] age, 36.3 [9.6] years; 295 012 female [50.1%]), and dispensing gap, 9 495 547 prescriptions for 516 790 patients (mean [SD] age, 37.7 [9.5]; 263 366 female [51.0%]). Laws were not associated with changes in the dispensing rate (0.11 patients per 1000; 95% CI, -0.30 to 0.52 patients per 1000), initiation rate (0.01 new patients per 1000; 95% CI, -0.04 to 0.06 new patients per 1000), or dispensing gap (-0.45 days; 95% CI, -0.97 to 0.08 days). Among states with high baseline prior authorization rejection rates, laws were associated with increases in the dispensing rate (0.29 patients per 1000; 95% CI, 0.07-0.51 patients per 1000) and initiation rate (0.06 new patients per 1000; 95% CI, 0.03-0.10 new patients per 1000) and with decreases in the dispensing gap (-0.91 days; 95% CI, -1.76 to -0.05 days).

Conclusions and relevance: This repeated cross-sectional study found that laws limiting prior authorization requirements for MOUD were only associated with increased buprenorphine dispensing, increased initiation, and timelier buprenorphine receipt when prior authorization requirements were frequent barriers to access.

Nguyen TD, Jiao YA, Lagisetty P, Bohnert AS, Conti RM, Chua KP

item.title: Deimplementing Race Adjustment in Clinical Algorithms and Decision Tools
item.description:
Importance: Many clinical decision support tools (CDSTs) incorporate race adjustment to tailor treatment based on a patient's race and ethnicity, contributing to racial and ethnic disparities in care. Mounting calls for race adjustment removal have resulted in some progress, yet the use of race adjustment in medicine persists.

Objective: To explore the processes, barriers, and facilitators to the implementation of race adjustment removal from 16 CDSTs and clinical information systems.

Design, setting, and participants: This qualitative study used the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) 2.0 to conduct virtual semistructured interviews with clinicians from different specialties at a multihospital academic health system from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024. An optional demographics survey was also sent to participants.

Main outcomes and measures: Patterns identified through thematic analysis informed by the CFIR 2.0 framework.

Results: Of the 44 identified clinicians, 32 (72.7%) completed an interview across 16 specialties. Of the 26 participants who reported their demographics, 14 (53.8%) were female, 6 (23.1%) were Asian, 1 (3.8%) were Hispanic or Latinx, 6 (23.1%) were non-Hispanic Black or African American, 13 (50%) were non-Hispanic White, 1 (3.8%) were multiracial or multiethnic, and 2 (7.9%) were other races or ethnicities (any other race or ethnicity). Thematic analysis of the interviews highlighted 5 generalizable themes: (1) clinicians varied greatly in their perceptions of race and race adjustment; (2) resistance, indifference, and unawareness remain key barriers to deimplementing race-based medicine; (3) race adjustment often serves as a harbinger of broader challenges with CDSTs; (4) consequences of race adjustment removal efforts remain understudied; and (5) national medical societies and multidisciplinary engagement are critical to overcoming implementation barriers.

Conclusions and relevance: In this qualitative study, cross-specialty perspectives yielded several critical barriers to deimplementing race adjustment in clinical medicine, alongside the identification of strategies required to drive change.

Jaffer M, Getachew Y, Chand M, Moore A, Keddem S, Ruggieri DG
Journal Article

item.title: Bone Mineral Density, FRAX Score, and Fracture Risk in Asian Adults With Type 2 Diabetes
item.description:
Importance: The recommendation of reducing the femoral neck (FN) bone mineral density (BMD) T score by 0.5 for fracture risk assessment in type 2 diabetes (T2D) is based primarily on data from White populations. Generalizability to Asian populations is unclear.

Objective: To evaluate associations of BMD and Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX) scores with fracture risk in Asians with T2D and the difference in FN BMD T score between those with vs without T2D at equal hip fracture risk.

Design, setting, and participants: This prospective cohort study using data from the Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study included adults 40 years of age or older with or without T2D recruited between 1995 and 2010. Data were captured until January 15, 2024, and analyzed in April 2025.

Exposures: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry-measured BMD T scores at the lumbar spine, FN, and total hip, and FRAX scores calculated using clinical risk factors and FN BMD.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcomes were hip fracture and major osteoporotic fracture (MOF). Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CIs.

Results: This cohort study consisted of 5817 adults (mean [SD] age, 61.3 [11.9] years; 4116 [70.76%] women). Of 629 participants with T2D, 107 (17.01%) experienced hip fractures, and 152 (24.17%) experienced MOFs during a mean (SD) follow-up period of 12.1 (7.2) years. HRs adjusted for age and sex per unit decrease in FN BMD T score were 1.57 (95% CI, 1.28-1.93) for hip fracture and 1.45 (95% CI, 1.22-1.72) for MOF. Higher FRAX score was also associated with an increased risk of hip fracture (HR, 1.07 [95% CI, 1.05-1.09] and MOF (HR, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.04-1.06]) in people with T2D. In addition, fracture incidence rates were higher in people with T2D than in those without T2D, with hip fracture rates of 13.27 vs 3.77 per 1000 person-years, respectively, and MOF rates of 19.92 vs 7.64 per 1000 person-years, respectively. For the same hip fracture risk at the same age, women with T2D had a higher FN BMD T score of 1.34 (95% CI, 0.69-1.98) and men of 0.47 (95% CI, 0.05-0.89) than those without T2D.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 5817 adults, BMD T score and FRAX score were associated with increased fracture risk in a population of Asian people with T2D. The magnitude of downward adjustment in BMD T score in Asians with T2D requires further external validation.

item.title: Parental Consent Requirements and Federally Funded Reproductive Health Care Among Texas Adolescents
item.description:
Importance: Since the 1970s, the federal Title X program has guaranteed confidential reproductive health care to young people in the US. A December 2022 court ruling, Alexander R. Deanda v Xavier Becerra et al, determined that Title X's confidentiality guarantees violated Texas state law regarding parental rights, thereby requiring parental consent for minors' contraceptive care.

Objective: To examine changes in patient volume, patient characteristics, and health care services received at Title X-funded health centers among Texas minors aged 17 years or younger compared with people aged 18 years in 2023 following implementation of the 2022 Deanda ruling.

Design, setting, and participants: This observational cohort study used a quasi-experimental pre-post design. The study included all visits that occurred between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023, among patients aged 18 years or younger receiving services at Title X-funded health centers in Texas. Data were analyzed between December 2024 and August 2026.

Exposure: Implementation in January 2023 of parental consent for contraception.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcome was the relative change in the number of patients and visits for minors (vs people aged 18 years) in the 1 year after the Deanda decision (2023) compared with the prior year (2022). Secondary outcomes included changes in the demographic profile of patients and in services received (eg, prescription contraception, leaving the visit with only condoms, sexually transmitted infection testing, or pregnancy testing). This study used difference-in-differences (DiD) Poisson regression analysis.

Results: Overall, 33 214 individuals (mean [SD] age, 16.3 [1.9] years; 27 040 female [81.4%]) were included in the analysis: 21 687 were aged 17 years or younger and 11 527 were aged 18 years. The number of individual minors decreased from 11 496 to 10 191 between 2022 and 2023 (percentage change, -11.4% [95% CI, -13.7% to -9.0%]); there was no statistically significant change among people aged 18 years (n = 5733 in 2022 and 5794 in 2023; percentage change, 1.1% [95% CI, -2.6% to 4.8%]). In DiD models, the 2022 to 2023 change in patient volume among minors was 9% lower relative to the corresponding change among people aged 18 years (multiplicative DiD, 0.91 [95% CI, 0.82 to 1.00]; P = .05). Compared with 2022, there were significantly fewer visits in 2023 among minors who were male compared with female (percentage change, -24.4% [95% CI, -28.7% to -20.0%] vs -7.4% [95% CI, -10.2% to -4.7%]; P < .001) and had limited English language proficiency compared with English proficiency (percentage change, -22.2% [95% CI, -26.5% to -17.9%] vs -7.7% [95% CI, -10.6% to -4.9%]; P < .001). There were no statistically significant differences in services received between minors and people aged 18 years before vs after the ruling.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, Texas minors' use of Title X-funded services decreased relative to people aged 18 years following the 2023 implementation of required parental consent for contraception. At a time when confidentiality protections for adolescents are under threat, these findings highlight how parental consent requirements interfere with access to reproductive health care.

item.title: Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement and Emergency Department Visits in Opioid Use: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Individuals receiving long-term opioid therapy (LTOT) have high rates of emergency department (ED) utilization, particularly for pain, addiction, and mental health (PAMH) conditions. Behavioral interventions that reduce reliance on acute care remain limited.

Objective: To evaluate whether Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE) is associated with ED utilization and ED-associated costs among veterans receiving LTOT.

Design, setting, and participants: Secondary analysis of electronic health record (EHR) data from a single-blind randomized clinical trial conducted from April 1, 2017 to October 1, 2021. Data were analyzed from March 2026 to May 2026. Participants were 185 veterans with chronic pain receiving LTOT with available EHR data.

Interventions: Participants were randomized 1 to 1 to mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement (mindfulness, reappraisal, and savoring training) or supportive psychotherapy, each delivered in 8 two-hour group sessions.

Main outcomes and measures: ED visits and ED-related costs during months 1 through 4, 5 through 8, and 9 through 12. ED visits were identified using US Department of Veterans Affairs EHR data and classified using all available diagnosis codes; costs were estimated using national emergency department expenditure data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey. Analyses were performed from March toSeptember 2026.

Results: The sample included 185 participants (mean [SD] age, 57.5 [11.7] years; 31 women [16.8%]). During months 9 to 12, mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement participants had 51 ED visits (0.54 visits per participant) compared with 65 ED visits (0.72 visits per participant) among supportive psychotherapy participants. Mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement was associated with fewer ED visits during months 9 to 12 compared with supportive psychotherapy (IRR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.13-0.65; P = .01), but not during earlier follow-ups. PAMH-associated ED visits during months 9 to 12 occurred at 0.17 visits per participant in the mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement group compared with 0.42 visits per participant in the supportive psychotherapy group; mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement was associated with fewer PAMH-related ED visits (IRR, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.07-0.74; P = .04). ED-associated costs during months 9 to 12 were $769.83 in the mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement group and $1043.33 in the supportive psychotherapy group; ED-related costs were lower in the mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement group for total ED visits and PAMH-related visits.

Conclusions and relevance: Among veterans receiving LTOT, mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement was associated with lower ED utilization and related costs during months 9 through 12 following treatment initiation but not during earlier follow-ups. Mindfulness-oriented recovery enhancement may be associated with decreased long-term acute care utilization and should be further evaluated for its health-system impact.

item.title: ABBV-CLS-7262 in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: ABBV-CLS-7262 is a central nervous system-penetrant eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2B activator that attenuates the integrated stress response (ISR).

Objective: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of ABBV-CLS-7262 in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Design, setting, and participants: ABBV-CLS-7262 was evaluated as a regimen of the HEALEY ALS Platform Trial, a placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized clinical trial conducted at 74 centers in the US between March 23, 2023, and October 3, 2024. Eligible participants with ALS were randomized to receive 1 of 2 doses of active drug or a matching placebo. The analysis included shared randomized participants receiving placebo from an additional regimen.

Intervention: Participants were randomized (2:1:1) to receive ABBV-CLS-7262 at a dosage of either 120 mg or 240 mg once daily or matching placebo for 24 weeks.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was rate of disease progression measured by ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) score and survival estimated together through a bayesian shared-parameter model relative to placebo. The primary comparison was between the 120-mg dose and placebo. The 240-mg dose was exploratory. Safety, secondary (eg, changes in ALSFRS-R total score, measures of limb and respiratory muscle strength, neurofilament light chain levels, quality of life, and cerebral spinal fluid [CSF] FGF21 levels, a putative biomarker of integrated stress response [ISR] pathway activity), and exploratory end points were also evaluated.

Results: In total, 335 participants were assigned to the ABBV-CLS-7262 regimen. Of them, 310 were randomized to receive ABBV-CLS-7262 (120-mg dose group: n = 155; 95 [61.3%] male; mean [SD] age, 57.3 [11.2] years; 240-mg dose group: n = 79; 49 [62.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 58.2 [11.0] years) and 76 to receive the regimen-specific placebo (42 [55.3%] male; mean [SD] age, 58.0 [11.1] years). An additional 50 participants were randomized to receive placebo from other concurrently enrolling regimens, bringing the total placebo group to 126 (81 [64.3%] male; mean [SD] age, 57.6 [11.7] years). Prespecified primary outcome analyses were performed comparing ABBV-CLS-7262 dose of 120 mg to the total shared placebo. The estimated median disease rate ratio common to the ALSFRS-R score and survival was 1.06 (95% credible interval, 0.85-1.32). The mean 24-week secondary outcome measures were not statistically significant between ABBV-CLS-7262 and placebo. The incidence rates of adverse events were similar between ABBV-CLS-7262 and placebo. No unexpected treatment-related risks were identified. CSF FGF21 levels decreased at week 24 in both ABBV-CLS-7262 dose groups compared with placebo (mean [SD] change from baseline, -6.8 [28.6] pg/mL for 120 mg, -8.3 [15.9] pg/mL for 240 mg, and 0.6 [11.1] pg/mL for placebo), consistent with central ISR pathway engagement and attenuation.

Conclusions and relevance: In this randomized clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of ABBV-CLS-7262 in ALS, ABBV-CLS-7262 attenuated the ISR but not ALS progression. This study also provides valuable ABBV-CLS-7262 safety and tolerability data.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04297683; NCT05740813.

item.title: State Abortion Bans and Neonatal and Infant Mortality in the US
item.description:
Importance: Following the US Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v Jackson Women's Health Organization (hereinafter Dobbs), many states implemented abortion bans. However, evidence of a possible association between state bans and neonatal and infant mortality remains limited, with prior studies constrained by short postban follow-up periods.

Objective: To examine the association between state-level abortion bans and neonatal and infant mortality in the US.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective population-based cohort study included all 50 US states and Washington, DC, and compared 16 states that implemented abortion bans with the 34 states and Washington, DC, without bans. The National Center for Health Statistics natality and mortality data were analyzed for neonatal mortality from January 1, 2012, to December 31, 2025, and for infant mortality from January 1, 2012, to December 31, 2024, using bayesian hierarchical Poisson models with a nonnegative matrix factorization-based counterfactual framework.

Exposure: State-level implementation of complete or 6-week abortion bans.

Main outcomes and measures: Neonatal mortality (deaths before 28 days of age) and infant mortality (deaths before 1 year of age), expressed per 1000 live births.

Results: Of 52 969 264 live births from 2012 through 2025, the analysis included 198 967 neonatal deaths through 2025 and 281 873 infant deaths through 2024. Of the infant deaths, 81 860 (29.0%) occurred among Black infants, 61 356 (21.8%) among Hispanic infants, 118 707 (42.1%) among White infants, and 7.1% among infants of other racial and ethnic groups. Across 16 states with bans, neonatal mortality increased by 5.5% (95% credible interval [CrI], 2.6%-8.5%), corresponding to approximately 745 (95% CrI, 367-1139) excess neonatal deaths in the states with bans; this estimate was attenuated after excluding Texas (2.2% [95% CrI, -0.5% to 5.2%]). There was an increase in infant mortality of 1.8% (95% CrI, -0.2% to 4.3%) in the postban periods, corresponding to approximately 288 (95% CrI, -25 to 658) excess deaths; although the 95% CrI included the null, the posterior probability of a positive association was approximately 0.95. Excluding Texas attenuated this estimate to near null (0.2% [95% CrI, -1.2% to 2.0%]). Increases in infant mortality were largest among Black infants (8.8% [95% CrI, 3.3%-14.2%]) and deaths due to congenital anomalies (6.9% [95% CrI, 1.8%-12.5%]). No individual state showed a statistically credible increase in infant mortality, although neonatal mortality increases were largest and most precisely estimated in Texas.

Conclusions and relevance: In this population-based cohort study of US live births, state abortion bans were associated with an increase in neonatal mortality and with inconclusive evidence of an increase in infant mortality. Findings suggest that abortion bans contribute to widening racial disparities in neonatal and infant mortality and highlight the importance of considering downstream perinatal health effects of restrictive abortion policies.

item.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulant Use and Acute Intracranial Hemorrhage in Adults Undergoing CT After Head Injury
item.description:
Importance: Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) therapy is commonly considered a risk factor for traumatic intracranial hemorrhage after head injury, but direct comparisons with no anticoagulation exposure are limited.

Objective: To assess whether active DOAC exposure, compared with no anticoagulation exposure, is associated with acute intracranial hemorrhage among adults undergoing computed tomography (CT) imaging after head injury.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study was conducted in 3 emergency departments within a large urban National Health Service trust in London, UK. Linked emergency department, hospital, and primary care prescribing records from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2022, were used. Adults aged 18 years or older presenting with head injury who underwent head CT were eligible. Analysis was conducted between June 2025 and June 2026.

Exposures: Active DOAC prescription (including apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, or rivaroxaban) at presentation compared with no anticoagulant prescription.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was acute intracranial hemorrhage on initial CT scan. Secondary outcomes were neurosurgical intervention and 28-day mortality. Associations were calculated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified confounders.

Results: This study included 11 401 episodes in 10 625 unique patients (6652 male [58.3%]; median age, 52 years [IQR, 33-77 years]). A total of 565 episodes (5.0%) occurred in participants prescribed DOAC therapy, and 10 836 episodes (95.0%) occurred in those with no anticoagulant exposure. Acute intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 40 DOAC-treated episodes (7.1%) and 831 non-anticoagulant-treated episodes (7.7%). After adjustment, DOAC exposure was not associated with acute intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.93; 95% CI, 0.70-1.21). Neurosurgical intervention occurred in 2 DOAC-treated episodes and 44 non-anticoagulant-treated episodes (0.4% in each group, AOR, 1.58; 95% CI, 0.47-4.17). Although crude 28-day mortality was higher among DOAC-treated episodes (17 of 565 [3.0%] vs 185 of 10 836 [1.7%]), adjusted analyses did not show higher odds of mortality (AOR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.46-1.01).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of adults undergoing CT imaging after head injury, DOAC exposure was not associated with higher adjusted odds of acute intracranial hemorrhage, neurosurgical intervention, or 28-day mortality compared with no anticoagulant exposure. However, clinically important differences cannot be excluded.

item.title: Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Biomarkers in the Decades Prior to a Cardiovascular Event
item.description:
Importance: Prior studies on trajectories of risk factors have typically focused on a single marker or did not study trajectories in association with cardiovascular events.

Objective: To evaluate sex- and age-specific trajectories of cardiovascular risk factors and circulating biomarkers associated with cardiovascular events and over the adult life course.

Design, setting, and participants: Longitudinal individual participant data from 4 cohort studies (Cardiovascular Health Study, Trøndelag Health Study, Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and Whitehall II) were pooled, covering a 34-year period (1985-2019). Analyses were conducted from April 2025 to September 2026.

Exposures: Repeatedly measured cardiovascular risk factors and circulating biomarkers (C-reactive protein, cardiac troponins, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide).

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was a composite of first-onset nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death. Linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models were used to estimate trajectories across individuals who experienced the primary outcome and those who survived and did not experience the primary outcome.

Results: In total, there were 316 719 study visits for 113 612 individuals without prior myocardial infarction or stroke, including 59 328 female individuals (52.2%; median [IQR] age at inclusion, 46 [33-61] years) and 54 284 male individuals (47.8%; median [IQR] age at inclusion, 45 [35-58] years). The primary outcome occurred in 8025 female individuals (13.5%) and 8892 male individuals (16.4%) during a median (IQR) follow-up of 18.9 (10.2-27.4) years. Individuals who experienced the primary outcome had less favorable cardiovascular risk factor trajectories and greater cumulative exposure than those who remained event free, with divergence evident up to 3 decades before the event. For instance, systolic blood pressure among female individuals was 4 mm Hg higher 3 decades before the event (121 mm Hg [95% CI, 119-123 mm Hg] vs 117 mm Hg [95% CI, 117-117 mm Hg]) and 7 mm Hg higher at time of the event or censoring (137 mm Hg [95% CI, 136-139 mm Hg] vs 130 mm Hg [95% CI, 129-130 mm Hg]). Similar long-term differences were observed in male individuals and for other cardiovascular risk factors. Cardiovascular biomarker trajectories began to diverge 1 to 3 decades before the event. For instance, differences in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide concentrations became apparent 1 decade before the event in both female (0.18 [95% CI, 0.07-0.30] SD log2 difference) and male (0.32 [95% CI, 0.21-0.42] SD log2 difference) individuals.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of individuals free from cardiovascular disease at baseline, trajectories of cardiovascular risk factors and biomarkers diverged between individuals who experienced the event and those who remained event free up to 3 decades before first-onset cardiovascular disease. These findings highlight the potential for earlier, life-course prevention strategies.

item.title: National Dissemination of a Decision Aid for Patients Considering a Left Ventricular Assist Device
item.description:
Importance: For patients with end-stage heart failure considering a left ventricular assist device (LVAD), shared decision-making is encouraged by guidelines and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Patients, caregivers, and clinicians have reported suboptimal guidance and support for LVAD decision-making, including a lack of unbiased educational materials.

Objective: To disseminate a tested patient decision aid (PDA) as standard practice in all LVAD programs across the US.

Design, setting, and participants: From 2018 to 2023, this I-DECIDE-LVAD initiative built a network of contacts across US CMS-certified LVAD programs to promote adoption and support implementation of the PDA to clinicians at LVAD programs and their patients considering an LVAD. Responses to all implementation assessments were collected and data analysis was conducted in October 2022 and mostly completed by January 2024.

Interventions: An LVAD PDA, consisting of a pamphlet and video, that was previously shown to improve decision quality.

Main outcomes and measures: This mixed-methods evaluation was guided by the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) framework, where an implementation assessment was collected among clinicians every 4 to 6 months; a subset of clinicians was interviewed and a subset of patients surveyed for a more comprehensive understanding of outcomes.

Results: Of 175 certified LVAD programs, all were successfully contacted and 169 (96.6%) adopted the PDAs. Over 4 years of follow-up, 156 programs responded to the implementation assessments; 123 (70.3%) reported active use, including 80 (45.7%) using the PDA as standard of care and 23 (13.1%) using it frequently. Overall, 7132 patients received the PDA, representing 83.2% of eligible patients at participating programs. Of the 205 patients who completed a survey across 16 programs (mean [SD] age, 62 [13] years; 50 females [24.4%]), 127 (62.0%) reported receiving the pamphlet and 79 (38.5%) received the video. Facilitators to PDA implementation included flexibility in how it could be used, positive opinions of and experiences with the PDA, and ease of integration within existing program structure. Common barriers included limited implementation capacity or preference for existing materials.

Conclusions and relevance: This nationwide quality improvement study of LVAD medical decision-making found that 70.3% of all LVAD programs in the US reported using a proven effective PDA with their patients. This initiative suggests that this is one of the broadest and most successful implementation efforts of a PDA.
